experiments.title: C2 campaign — RFdiffusion3
experiments.verdict_detail: The campaign's record counts 18 designs and 90 samples across two batches; the fold runs that survive in this workspace are listed in the generation chapters. Closed as a negative: the generator was replaced (Genie 3) and the acceptance bar moved from 0.6 to 0.8.
experiments.summary: The first attempt at the released problem: RFdiffusion3 backbones, Boltz-2 folds, IPSAE screening — closed as a negative. Every recorded design and score kept below.
experiments.goal: Run the released TNF-α problem end to end with RFdiffusion3 as the generator: generate, fold, screen, and judge against the challenge's objectives. The campaign is the baseline the Genie 3 campaign is measured against.
goal_extra: The brief ranks three objectives: (1) pH-selective human binding (bind at 7.4, none at 6.0), (2) mouse cross-reactivity, (3) affinity.
This campaign tests the first generator (RFdiffusion3) against objective 3 (binding) only — and produced no submission candidate.
Its negative result set the rules for the Genie 3 campaign: full-backbone re-sequencing, the 0.8 acceptance line, and mouse-first selection.

chapters.title: Generation — RFdiffusion3
chapters.text: RFdiffusion3 (the released checkpoint) generated binder backbones against the released TNF-α problem, in two batches (w1/w2) around the B102/D62 junction and the human groove.

steps.title: Batch w1 + w2
steps.text: Backbones under hotspot constraints; several models per design id.

chapters.title: Folding — Boltz-2 on the local GPU
chapters.text: Each candidate co-folded with the human TNF-α construct: 5 diffusion samples per design, seed 42, on the local RTX 5070.

steps.title: Five samples per design
steps.text: The fold is a distribution over poses; the spread across samples is read, not the best row alone.

chapters.title: Screening — IPSAE at the designed site
chapters.text: IPSAE scored every sample at the designed interface (10 Å PAE cutoff); the bar: ipSAE >= 0.6 AND pDockQ2 >= 0.23. Later recalibrated: the submission line moved to 0.8.

steps.title: Score every sample
steps.text: fold_metrics.csv per run; the at-site check distinguishes a real interface from an off-site pose.

chapters.outcome: 0 of 18 designs cleared the bar at the designed site.

chapters.title: Outcome — the negative, and what it taught
chapters.text: The campaign closed as a documented negative: good iPTM, weak interfaces. The lesson shaped everything after: generator choice dominates (Genie 3 8/23 vs RFdiffusion3 1/40 on the calibration), and the acceptance line belongs at 0.8.

steps.title: Recorded, not discarded
steps.text: Every design stays in the table below with its score — the negative is part of the campaign's evidence.

experiments.title: Genie 3 campaign — the night run
experiments.summary: One campaign, one methodology (Genie 3 → ProteinMPNN → Boltz-2 → IPSAE), several experiments: 279 designs, from the first 0.25 to the submission set. Every design and score below, experiment by experiment.
experiments.goal: Take the one productive backbone (d7, from Genie 3) and run experiments on it — re-sequencing, dual-species selection, directed evolution, and finally the histidine retrofit for the pH switch. Each experiment answers one objective; they are the sections below.
goal_extra: The brief ranks three objectives: (1) pH-selective human binding (bind at 7.4, none at 6.0), (2) mouse cross-reactivity, (3) affinity — all three on one molecule.
This experiment answers all three: sr2-ds-mce-14-v6-r2c — human 0.849, mouse 0.847 (both 5/5 at the designed site), pH switch +1.738 (54.7x toward 7.4).
Every experiment has its own section: re-sequencing, mouse-first selection, directed evolution, and the histidine retrofit that flipped the switch.
All numbers are in-silico (Boltz-2, IPSAE, PROPKA); no wet-lab data exists.

chapters.title: Calibration — the bars
chapters.summary: The released campaign re-scored through our pipeline: sets every bar the campaign used.
chapters.goal: Before designing anything, the released Anthropic/Adaptyv campaign (150 TNF-α designs, 13 wet-lab binders) was re-scored with our own Boltz-2 + IPSAE pipeline. This fixed the acceptance bars: ipSAE >= 0.8 for submission-grade, mouse cross-reactivity tracks tightness, and the pipeline itself reproduces the released numbers within ±0.03.

steps.title: Re-score six released designs
steps.text: Three wet-lab winners and three high-scoring losers folded with the standard protocol. Their ipsae_min_boltz2 reproduced within ±0.03.

steps.title: Read the outcomes
steps.text: The 0.6-0.7 band produced 0/22 binders; >= 0.8 bound at ~26%. Two never-bound designs outscored every winner — the metric is rank-grade, never a promise.

chapters.text: The bars came from released wet-lab data (filter-calibration): ipSAE 0.8 / pDockQ2 0.23 as the line, 0.6 as the do-not-discard floor - the 0.6-0.7 band bound nothing in that dataset.

chapters.title: Generation — Genie 3
chapters.summary: 8 Genie 3 designs on the released problem; CA-only sequences capped at 0.25 — the backbone survived.
chapters.goal: Generate binders for the released TNF-α problem (hotspots B102 + D62) with Genie 3, then re-sequence and fold. This generation exposed the CA-only ProteinMPNN trap and produced the d7 backbone that everything later builds on.

steps.title: Generate 8 designs
steps.text: Genie 3 (aqlaboratory, 347 MB checkpoint) on the BinderBench problem 10_tnfa. All 8 placed on the designed interface.

steps.title: CA-only re-sequencing
steps.text: ProteinMPNN on CA atoms only — every sequence capped at 0.248 ipSAE. The trap: sequence design needs the full backbone.

steps.title: The lesson
steps.text: Re-sequence the FOLDED backbone with full-backbone ProteinMPNN instead. That fix is what produced the d7 family.

chapters.text: One methodology throughout: Genie 3 backbones, ProteinMPNN sequences, Boltz-2 co-folds, IPSAE scoring - the first batches against the campaign's hotspot sets.
chapters.outcome: The first families land around 0.25 at-site ipSAE.

chapters.title: The d7 family
chapters.summary: Full-backbone re-sequencing of the folded d7 backbone: 18 variants 0.63-0.85, champion d7x-t3-3.
chapters.goal: Take the d7 backbone's FOLDED conformation and re-sequence it with vanilla full-backbone ProteinMPNN. The family converged: one backbone, many sequences, all at the designed interface.

steps.title: Extract the folded backbone
steps.text: Chain A of the d7 fold becomes the template.

steps.title: Re-sequence with ProteinMPNN
steps.text: vanilla v_48_020, T = 0.1/0.3, several seeds — 18 variants.

steps.title: Fold and screen
steps.text: Every variant co-folded (Boltz-2, 5 samples, seed 42) and screened at the designed two-protomer junction. Champion: d7x-t3-3 (0.832-0.852).

chapters.text: Round 2: the d7 family resequenced with ProteinMPNN - the first designs in the winners' zone (best at-site ipSAE 0.248, crossing D/C).
chapters.outcome: The d7 family becomes the working scaffold.

chapters.title: Directed evolution
chapters.summary: Fixed-position mutation around the champions: D47A lifts the record to 0.871; generation 2 converged.
chapters.goal: Mutate the best family members directly (ProteinMPNN with 3 free positions per variant), fold, and keep what improves. The RF-style loop: each generation mutates the winners of the last and re-selects.

steps.title: Generation 1
steps.text: 24 variants around d7x-t3-3 / d7x-t3-1 / m1-d7b-3. e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6 = champion + ONE substitution (D47A) -> 0.871, the human record.

steps.title: Generation 2
steps.text: Mutants of v6 and the tight d7 members. Converged: no design beat v6; e2-e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6-v2 joined the ladder.

chapters.text: Directed evolution: fixed-position ProteinMPNN around the d7 pockets; the ladder climbs within the family.

chapters.title: Mouse check + calibration
chapters.summary: The family keeps the designed interface on mouse but degraded; the released mouse binders set the band (0.73-0.89).
chapters.goal: The challenge requires mouse cross-reactivity. Every candidate folded against the mouse construct (aligned window, P06804 85-235). The released mouse-binding winners were folded through the same pipeline to calibrate what a real cross-reactive binder reads.

steps.title: Build the mouse target
steps.text: Human 82-233 -> mouse 85-235 by alignment; the designed site remaps to positions 107 + 67 (human H68 -> mouse Y).

steps.title: Fold the candidates
steps.text: The champions keep the designed interface on mouse but ~0.2 lower; the released mouse binders hold their human scores (0.73-0.89) — our family sat below that band.

steps.title: The fix
steps.text: Cross-reactivity must be selected for, not checked for. Next generation: select on mouse.

chapters.text: The mouse cross-check: the family's top designs folded against the mouse construct to read the species gap before redesigning for it.
chapters.outcome: The species gap measured; the mce design follows.

chapters.title: Mouse-directed redesign
chapters.summary: The d7 backbone re-sequenced and selected ON mouse: mce-14 is the first dual-species hit.
chapters.goal: Re-sequence the d7 backbone (64 sequences) and fold the top 16 against MOUSE first. Select on the harder target; confirm human after. mce-14 came out of this: mouse 0.704-0.847 and human 0.693-0.852, both 5/5 at the designed junction.

steps.title: Generate + select on mouse
steps.text: 64 ProteinMPNN sequences; the 16 best-predicted folded against mouse.

steps.title: One hit
steps.text: mce-14: the only candidate reaching the mouse band. Human retention confirmed on the same binder.

steps.title: Visual check
steps.text: mce-14 hugs the trimer the same way on both species — the pose of the good designs.

chapters.text: Mouse-directed redesign (mce): resequencing toward the mouse-conserved contacts.

chapters.title: Dual-select generation 1
chapters.summary: Mutants of the dual hits: five dual hits; ds-mce-14-v6 (T48S) beats its parent on both targets.
chapters.goal: Fixed-position mutants of mce-14 / m1-d7b-3 / v6, selected with the mouse-first cascade (mouse fold -> promote >= 0.7 -> human confirmation).

steps.title: Mouse stage
steps.text: All five mce-14 mutants hold mouse at 5/5 (0.839-0.863); one m1-d7b-3 mutant promoted.

steps.title: Human stage
steps.text: All six promoted designs fold 5/5 at-site. ds-mce-14-v6 (one substitution, T48S) = mouse 0.854 / human 0.856 — beats the parent on BOTH targets.

chapters.text: Dual-select generation 1: selection pressure on the human and mouse reads together (the ds lineage).

chapters.title: Dual-select generation 2
chapters.summary: One step deeper: seven dual hits; ds2-mce-14-v7-v1 sets the mouse record (0.868); combined plateau reached.
chapters.goal: The same cascade around the three best dual designs. The render-based tie-breaker fired on one borderline design (perched pose -> excluded).

steps.title: Mouse stage
steps.text: 8 of 9 mutants >= 0.847 at-site; ds2-mce-14-v7-v1 = new mouse record 0.868.

steps.title: Human stage
steps.text: All seven promoted fold 5/5 (0.824-0.842). No design beats ds-mce-14-v6's combined profile: the family has plateaued.

chapters.text: Dual-select generation 2: a second round of combined selection.
chapters.outcome: No combined improvement over the ds-14-v6 line (ds2-mce-14-v7-v1 kept for the ladder).

chapters.title: pH linkage check — the missing objective
chapters.summary: The family has no pH switch — its natural linkage runs the wrong way (tighter at pH 6.0).
chapters.goal: The challenge ranks pH-selective binding FIRST. The vendored PROPKA linkage scorer (validated blind on FcRn) measured the binding-linked proton release of five lineage folds. All negative: the wrong direction.

steps.title: Score the family
steps.text: delta_log_Ka from -0.11 to -0.99 — every design binds more in acid. Objective 1 unclaimable.

steps.title: The mechanism to retrofit
steps.text: A histidine facing a positively charged target residue: neutral at 7.4 (binds), +1 at 6.0 (repelled).

chapters.text: The pH layer measured with PROPKA and the Wyman linkage: does the lineage carry a switch?
chapters.outcome: No switch in the lineage - recorded negative; the retrofit follows.

chapters.title: The switch — his retrofit + E33H
chapters.summary: Histidine retrofit flips the linkage; the E33H single substitution gives the best design: human 0.849 / mouse 0.847 / switch 54.7x.
chapters.goal: Retrofit the upstream campaign's switch mechanism onto backbones that actually dock: histidines placed facing the interface cations (found in the fold geometry). Round 1 flipped the sign at a binding cost; the alternative-position scan found E33H — a salt-bridge residue converted into the switch — with binding intact on both species.

steps.title: Round 1 — the sign flips
steps.text: Nine His mutants; the best (G45H+L37H+S48H) reads +0.877 (7.5x toward 7.4) at a binding cost of ~0.15-0.2.

steps.title: The b-class survives mouse
steps.text: sr1-mce-14-b: human 0.659 / mouse 0.703, both 5/5, switch +0.836.

steps.title: Recovery generations
steps.text: Whole-chain resampling (sr3/sr4) collapsed — recorded negative. The reversion scan (sr6) localized the cost to H37.

steps.title: E33H — the winner
steps.text: Converting the Glu33 salt bridge into a histidine: sr2-ds-mce-14-v6-r2c reads human 0.849 / mouse 0.847 / switch +1.738 (54.7x) — all three objectives, one molecule.

chapters.text: Histidine switch retrofit (sr1): E33H - the linkage sign flips on paper.
chapters.outcome: sr1 carries the engineered linkage; the pH objective stays open.

chapters.title: The d12 family — second scaffold
chapters.summary: The independent scaffold from Genie 3 batch 2: strong human interfaces, but mouse-weak.
chapters.goal: Batch 2 (16 Genie 3 designs) was screened the same way; its best backbone (d12, 92-residue binder) was re-sequenced and folded. It passes both legs of the original bar but drops on mouse (0.426) — kept as the independent backup family.

steps.title: Batch 2 screening
steps.text: 16 designs; the d12 backbone re-sequenced with full-backbone ProteinMPNN.

steps.title: The mouse verdict
steps.text: b2x-d12-2: human 0.788 / mouse 0.426 — human-context only; the d7 lineage carries the dual objective.

chapters.text: A second family (d12): scores 0.62-0.83, every sequence 5/5 at the designed leg; d12-2 buries 311 atom pairs.
chapters.outcome: A second working scaffold next to d7.

chapters.title: Mining-01 — the d7 plateau
chapters.summary: 80 further sequences on both backbones: plateau per the pre-registered rules; two members entered the ladder.
chapters.goal: After the families were established: broaden the sequence space (d7 at T = 0.1/0.3/0.5, d12 at 0.1/0.3), 20 folded. Outcome: no new best >= 0.85 and no worst-fold >= 0.80 — plateau; the d7 family now holds ~30 members.

steps.title: Sample wide
steps.text: 80 sequences across two backbones and three temperatures.

steps.title: Plateau
steps.text: Best new 0.837 (< 0.85 bar). m1-d7b-3 and m1-d7a-4 joined the ladder; the family ceiling was measured.

chapters.text: Mining-01 (pre-registered): 80 further sequences across both families.
chapters.outcome: Two mining members entered the ladder.

chapters.title: Mining-02 — fresh backbones
chapters.summary: The four best untreated backbones re-sequenced: no design reached 0.80 — those backbones are closed.
chapters.goal: Pre-registered search on four fresh backbones (b2-d14, b2-d11, b2-d10, genie3-d0). 24 designs folded. FAIL/STOP per the rules: best 0.599 at-site. No third family exists in the first two batches.

steps.title: Fresh backbones only
steps.text: The four best untreated backbones from both Genie 3 batches, vanilla MPNN, top-6 folded each.

steps.title: Closed
steps.text: Best: 0.599 at-site (5/5) — a near-miss. Recorded; the two families stand as the only productive scaffolds.

chapters.text: Mining-02 (pre-registered): the four best untreated backbones resequenced.
chapters.outcome: Logged; no new head above the ladder.

chapters.title: RBS batch-03 + redesign
chapters.summary: Targeting our own campaign's receptor-binding site: the junction never scores; the r3x redesign confirmed it.
chapters.goal: A test of the alternative epitope (the campaign's own RBS junction): 12 Genie 3 designs at hotspots 78/82/84 + 142, then a full-backbone redesign (r3x, 18 folds). CA-only scores 0.02-0.23; the redesign did not rescue it.

steps.title: RBS batch
steps.text: 12 designs on the campaign's junction; winner-scale interfaces but low scores.

steps.title: r3x redesign
steps.text: Full-backbone re-sequencing on the three best backbones — still negative. The released problem's surface is the productive one.

chapters.text: RBS batch-03 + redesign: the RBS epitope retried under the fixed protocol.
chapters.outcome: The RBS negative holds; the campaign closes on the submission lineage.
